guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE for third-party access to resources for a user. Registering an application is required first. read_api is the least-privilege documented scope that covers read access to the issues API. The connected person's existing project access bounds the results, and access tokens expire after two hours by default, so refresh tokens are needed. Paginated reads use page and per_page, with keyset pagination available on the project issues endpoint. Setup and execution are untested.

findings.title: Authorization code with PKCE is documented for user-authorized third-party access
findings.detail: GitLab supports authorization code with PKCE and authorization code flows. PKCE is recommended for both client and server apps. The app redirects the user to /oauth/authorize with requested scopes and exchanges the returned code at /oauth/token.
findings.appliesWhen: Individual customer accounts connect through OAuth, as the confirmed request states.

evidence.quote: Authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) :
Most secure. Without PKCE, you’d have to include client secrets on mobile clients.
This flow is recommended for both client and server apps.

findings.title: read_api grants read access to the API including projects
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects. It is the documented read-only API scope; read_user alone covers only the profile and user endpoints. The token inherits the connected person's access, so only projects that person can access are returned.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading issue titles through the REST issues endpoints for projects the connected person can access.

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.
Scope Access read_api Grants read access to the API. Sufficient for queries.
The access token allows you to make requests to the API on behalf of a user.

findings.title: Register an OAuth application and configure its credentials and redirect URI first
findings.detail: Authorization code flows require the application to be registered first in user settings or group settings. Registration provides an Application ID and Client Secret, and the redirect URI must match the one used in authorization and token requests.
findings.appliesWhen: Before the first test of the OAuth authorization path.

findings.title: Access tokens expire after two hours and need refresh tokens
findings.detail: By default, access tokens expire after two hours (7200 seconds). Integrations must use the refresh_token attribute to obtain new tokens. Refresh tokens remain usable after the access token expires. Self-managed administrators can change the token lifetime.
findings.appliesWhen: Ongoing reads after the initial authorization.

steps.title: Register a GitLab OAuth application for the integration
steps.detail: In GitLab, create an OAuth application for the user (or group) that will connect. Enter a name and redirect URI, select read_api as the scope, and save. GitLab then provides an Application ID and a Client Secret. Use a self-hosted instance URL as the host if the customer does not use gitlab.com.

steps.title: Prepare PKCE values and the consent URL
steps.detail: Generate a state value, a code verifier (43-128 characters) and a S256 code challenge. Build the authorization URL with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state, scope=read_api and the code challenge. The customer user opens it and approves access; GitLab redirects back with a code. Verify that the returned state equals the one sent before exchanging the code.
steps.doneWhen: A consent URL is built with the documented parameters and the state value is stored for callback comparison.

steps.title: Read the next page of issue titles
steps.detail: Follow the next link from the previous Link header. Replace the placeholder with the literal next URL from the prior response; resolve any relative href against the same HTTPS instance host. Repeat until the Link header has no rel="next" entry, which is the documented end condition. Keep the Authorization header on every request. Use the literal <NEXT_PAGE_URL> from the previous response's Link header as the full curl URL. The documented end condition is that the Link header is absent and the array is empty.
steps.doneWhen: Each page is read in order and the walk stops when no rel="next" link is returned. A response without a rel="next" Link header marks the end of the listing. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
